name: HC-SR04
description: 4-pin ultrasonic distance module measuring roughly 2 cm to 400 cm with about 3 mm resolution. A 10 us pulse on Trig starts a burst of eight 40 kHz cycles; the module then drives Echo high for a duration proportional to the round-trip time, and distance is derived from the speed of sound (distance_cm = echo_us / 58). It runs from 5 V and uses simple GPIO timing rather than a serial bus. The default low-cost rangefinder for hobby robotics and obstacle avoidance.

pins.name: Trig
pins.description: trigger input; a 10 us high pulse starts a measurement

pins.name: Echo
pins.description: echo output; 5 V pulse whose width equals the round-trip ultrasonic time

typical_application: Obstacle avoidance and distance sensing for robots, parking/proximity alerts, liquid level and presence detection.
gotchas: the Echo output is a 5 V signal - feed a 3.3 V MCU through a voltage divider or level shifter to avoid damaging the GPIO
the module needs a true 5 V supply; running VCC below ~4.5 V gives erratic or no readings
leave at least ~60 ms between measurements so the previous echo does not bleed into the next reading
soft, angled, or sound-absorbing surfaces scatter the burst and cause missed/false echoes; the beam is narrow (~15 deg)
if Echo never goes low (no object within range), add a timeout in firmware or the read will block
minimum reliable distance is ~2 cm; closer objects fall inside the transducer ring-down dead zone
